description: A stone wall of wall_width × wall_height × thickness, cut into exactly `pieces` Voronoi pieces, falls and comes to rest on the ground (rbd_settle). The crack centres spread evenly over the wall (a jittered R2 sequence; seed moves them) and crowd towards the hit point as impact grows, so the pieces are smaller there. The hit lands in the middle of the wall from -Z and throws the pieces near it away; every piece also gets a random tip and slide to one side, so the wall comes down in a heap at its foot even with impact 0 (cut pieces of a wall, stacked, would otherwise stand). intact is the standing wall already cut, broken the pieces at rest. Dressed faces are weathered stone, broken faces (group inside) raw stone; uv run in metres on the standing wall, so the grain moves with each piece.

pieces.label: pieces
pieces.desc: how many pieces it breaks into

impact.label: impact
impact.desc: how hard the wall is hit in its middle (from -Z); 0 lets it collapse

seed.label: seed
seed.desc: random seed of the cracks and the fall

sites.note: one crack centre per piece: an even spread (R2 sequence, jittered) pulled towards the hit by impact, so pieces are smaller there

cracked.note: 0.5 mm gap: rbd_settle takes pieces that touch exactly as starting inside each other and pushes them apart (a warning)

mapped.note: uv in metres on the standing wall, so the grain moves with each piece

weathered.note: the dressed faces: soft, low-contrast blotches

grit.note: the broken faces: fine, high-contrast grain

standing_count.note: counts the connected pieces into a detail attribute: the assert expr cannot compare with the var pieces (its own piece count of that name comes first)

standing_whole.note: the pieces fill the wall but for their 0.5 mm gap: tolerance 0.0005 × surface area

loosened.note: the pieces moved apart a little (in the wall plane), so none starts propped up by its neighbours

params.code:
const c = prim(0, 'class', pointprims(0, @ptnum)[0]), s = point(1, 'P', c);
@P = add(@P, [s.x * 0.05, s.y * 0.05, 0]);

kick.note: per piece (class = its crack centre): the hit throws the pieces near it away from -Z, every piece tips and slumps to a random side so the wall falls

rest_count.note: counts the connected pieces into a detail attribute: the assert expr cannot compare with the var pieces (its own piece count of that name comes first)

whole.note: moved rigidly: same stone as the wall but for the 0.5 mm gap (0.0005 × surface area)

rest.note: 1 cm: contact slop of the solver

params.names: part piece_count v w settled contacts

broken.label: Broken
broken.description: The pieces where they come to rest on the ground: `pieces` closed convex pieces (prim name pieceN and class N, the same in both outputs), outer faces in stone, broken faces (prim group inside) in raw_stone, with uv in metres.

intact.label: Intact
intact.description: The wall standing before it falls, already cut into the same pieces with the same names, materials and uv: for a before/after switch or another simulation.
